should_fail.message: Here is a 6-slide deck on choosing a pgvector index: the index definitions and a sample query as code, a comparison table of HNSW, IVFFlat and exact search, and every figure badged measured or untested.

deck_spec.title: Choosing a pgvector Index for Semantic Search
deck_spec.audience: Backend engineers adding semantic search to a Postgres application
deck_spec.purpose: Help the team choose a pgvector index by comparing HNSW, IVFFlat and exact search on speed, recall and build cost
deck_spec.argument: HNSW answers fastest at the highest recall in the benchmark, IVFFlat is the cheaper fallback and exact search only suits small tables; the HNSW build time at full size is still untested
deck_spec.call_to_action: Use HNSW for the search feature, and time a full-size index build before the launch
narrative_arc: Open on the choice: which pgvector index to use for semantic search
Compare HNSW, IVFFlat and exact search side by side
Show the index definitions and a sample query as code
Report what the benchmark measured and what is still untested
Close with the recommendation and the next steps

resolved_data.synthesis: On 1 million 768-dimension embeddings HNSW answered in 4 ms at 98% recall, IVFFlat in 9 ms at 92% recall and exact search in 310 ms. The 2-hour estimate for building the HNSW index on 10 million rows is untested.

slides.purpose: Open the deck: choosing a pgvector index for semantic search
slides.content_brief: Cover slide with the title 'Choosing a pgvector Index for Semantic Search' and a subtitle naming the three options: HNSW, IVFFlat and exact search
slides.assumes: The audience knows the application stores its embeddings in Postgres
slides.hands_off: The index choice decides how fast and how accurate the search is

slides.purpose: Compare the three ways to search the embeddings
slides.content_brief: Comparison table of HNSW, IVFFlat and exact search, one row per option, with columns for query time, recall, build cost and memory; a one-line takeaway beneath: HNSW is the fastest at the highest recall, and costs the most to build
slides.assumes: The audience has heard of approximate nearest-neighbour search
slides.hands_off: HNSW leads on speed and recall; its build cost is the price

slides.purpose: Show how each index is defined
slides.content_brief: Code listing of the index definitions: enable the vector extension, create an HNSW index with its m and ef_construction settings, and the IVFFlat alternative with its lists setting; two short bullets on what each setting trades
slides.hands_off: Each index is one statement, and its settings trade build cost for recall

slides.purpose: Show a nearest-neighbour query and how to tune it
slides.content_brief: Code listing of a sample query that orders the rows by cosine distance to a query embedding and returns the top 10, with the ef_search setting above it, and a one-line note beneath on raising ef_search for recall
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the index definitions
slides.hands_off: One query and one setting control the speed-recall trade at search time

slides.content_brief: Three stat cards from the benchmark on 1 million 768-dimension embeddings, each badged measured: HNSW at 4 ms and 98% recall, IVFFlat at 9 ms and 92% recall, and exact search at 310 ms
slides.assumes: The audience has seen the options and how each is queried
slides.hands_off: HNSW was the fastest and the most accurate in the benchmark

slides.purpose: Close with the recommendation, what is still untested and the next steps
slides.content_brief: Recommend HNSW for the search feature; badge the estimated 2 hours to build it on 10 million rows as untested; then the next steps in order: build the index on a full-size copy, time the build, tune ef_search, then launch; end with the call to action
slides.assumes: The audience has seen what the benchmark measured
slides.hands_off: Choose HNSW, and time a full-size build before the launch
